archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide aggro that kills by trigger, not by combat. deck-audit matches aggro from strategic_frame.json and every structural axis agrees: 30 creatures inside the 26-32 band, 37 land copies, threat-density 11 against a floor of 3. The frame is right about what this deck is. The sixteen swaps moved it off the aristocrats build the commander is usually given and onto the entry-trigger build, and the artifacts now describe one deck rather than two.
verdict: This is a genuinely good linear deck with two thin classes, and the order between them has to be argued rather than counted. The bodies arrive — a lord or anthem in 83.2% of games, a token multiplier in 78.2% — and stack 009 verified the plan they feed: one {B}{B} Vampire through one doubler and three payoffs is nine triggers and 12 damage at every seat. The payoff half binds. Four cards convert a creature entry into each-opponent damage, 25.8% of opening sevens, and the joint go-wide kill is 40.2% assembled and 27.5% by turn six. The noncreature answer is thinner still on raw draw odds — two cards, 13.7% of openers, and functionally one against a cheap permanent — but it is second because of what each gap costs. A missing payoff is paid in every game and drops the deck onto combat into ~120 life behind three defences. A missing answer is paid only when an opponent presents the permanent, and the trigger plan routes around most of what that permanent would do.

single_points_of_failure.why: Not a single point — four cards — but the class gating the deck's primary kill. Four copies is 25.8% of an opening seven; the corpus's next step, five copies, is 31%. open_questions.question: Does Mirkwood Bats trigger once per token when a single token-creation event is doubled by Anointed Procession, Mondrak or Elspeth — i.e. does one eminence trigger under two doublers cause four life loss at each seat, or one?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between a fifth converter that compounds with the deck's three replacement-effect doublers and a flat one-per-event drip. The whole case for the add rests on which it is, and stacks 002 and 008 already established the doubled-event board this would be resolved on.

open_questions.question: Olivia's Wrath resolving on the deck's own board: is Purphoros a creature for the -X/-X, does killing your own creatures change X or your devotion mid-resolution, and do Cathars' Crusade counters already on Corpse Knight and Mondrak survive it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Five of thirty creatures are non-Vampires — Corpse Knight (a converter), Mondrak (a doubler), Abzan Falconer, Ocelot Pride and Purphoros. Nobody has priced the deck's one-sided sweeper against the deck, and the answer decides whether it stays.

open_questions.question: What does the GO-WIDE KILL rate become with a fifth entry-trigger payoff in the any_of group?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The binding claim in this diagnosis is that the payoff class at 4 gates the primary kill at 27.5% by turn six. Adding the candidate to goldfish_targets.json and re-simulating measures the delta directly instead of inferring it from the hypergeometric.

open_questions.question: Does the Reconnaissance line work as the primer claims — remove attacking Vampires from combat after Edgar's attack trigger and Sanctum Seeker's attack triggers have resolved, keeping the +1/+1 counters and the drain?
open_questions.why_it_matters: deck_recon.json carries it as a one-source claim about this exact shell. If it holds, a one-mana white enchantment converts every attack into a free drain with no combat risk, which is a different kind of add from anything in the list above. Nothing in this repo has verified it.

open_questions.question: Does the corpus support a rule for ranking two thin classes against each other when one gates the win and the other gates a contingency — and for pricing noncreature-answer depth in a linear deck that is AT its interaction template rather than over it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The corrected count is seven real answers against an aggro template of 5-6, so the order between the payoff class and the noncreature answer no longer follows from over-investment. It now rests on a substitution argument — trigger damage routes around the permanents the answers exist for — which is reasoning this diagnosis makes rather than quotes. The frame's own gaps list names the same hole: there is no section on trigger-based kills versus combat kills.

gaps: The interaction axis counts role tags, and in this deck five of its twelve cards are not answers: Impact Tremors, Purphoros and Warleader's Call carry removal:damage for text that damages each opponent, Boros Charm for a mode that hits players, and Elspeth for a conditional -3. deck-audit says as much sideways — the payoff component's shared_axes is ["interaction"] — but nothing in the pipeline nets it out, and the interaction-breadth by_class counts inherit the same over-read. The first pass of this diagnosis took the 12 on trust and built an argument on it.

The colour delta of the Brightclimb Pathway swap could not be measured. mana_analysis.json is tracked and this artifact is read-only, so the on-curve rates for the changed base were not computed. Running mana-analysis after the swap would settle it.

goldfish_targets.json declares only entry-triggered conversion. Bontu's Monument (cast trigger), Sanctum Seeker (attack trigger) and Throne of the God-Pharaoh (end step, tapped creatures) also convert width into each-opponent life loss and are in no any_of group, so the measured 52.5% is the rate for the doubler-composing subset, not for conversion as such.
considering.json and tutor_guide.json are stale against this decklist and were deliberately not read or cited.

The synergy graph contributes nothing here: all 33 intra-deck edges are lands pointing at Herald's Horn under one Ramp + Cost Reduction rule, and its pool candidates for this deck are an aura package (All That Glitters, Ethereal Armor, Hyena Umbra) that belongs to a different archetype. deck-facts says why — it is a format-wide top-10 shortlist, not a fit score.

The strategy corpus has no section on token doubling as a multiplicative resource, on converting board width into non-combat damage, or on typal critical mass. This deck's entire plan is those three things, so every axis reading above is borrowed from adjacent sections.

deck_recon.json is dated as_of 2026-08-03 and two of the six adds lean on it. Several of its findings — Command Tower, Cavern of Souls, Charismatic Conqueror, Anguished Unmaking, Warleader's Call, Impact Tremors, Elspeth, Caretaker's Talent, Legion's Landing — have already been applied, so the remaining findings are what is left of a pass that was largely consumed.

No opposing-interaction model exists. Every assembly rate quoted is from a goldfish that simulates resource development with no removal and no sweeper, which is exactly the axis (card-advantage after a wrath) this diagnosis calls the second weakness.

No candidate was found for a one-shot width-to-drain burst (Malakir Bloodwitch was proposed and withdrawn). goldfish_targets.json declares no component such a card could join, so its value cannot be grounded against anything this repo measures — it would need a declared any_of group first.

findings.note: The Abzan Falconer cut is justified on a false premise about the deck's own cards. The `why` says its flying grant is 'conditional on +1/+1 counters, which arrive from Edgar's attack trigger — i.e. after you have already committed to combat.' Counters do not principally arrive from Edgar's attack trigger. Cathars' Crusade is in the mainboard of cards.json and reads 'Whenever a creature you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control' — an entry-based, pre-combat source that fires on every eminence token and every Vampire cast, which is the deck's core event. Vampire Socialite has every other Vampire ENTER with an additional counter, and Elspeth's 0 puts a counter on each creature you control. So the whole board is flying before attackers are declared, not after. The entry's own `cost_of_cutting` names the card that refutes its `why` ('Cathars' Crusade plus Falconer is a real two-card sky'), so the two halves of the entry disagree. Two aggravating facts: strategic_frame.json carries this exact interaction as an UNRESOLVED rules question ('Cathars' Crusade into Abzan Falconer: does one doubled entry give the whole board flying?'), which this diagnosis does not carry forward into open_questions; and Abzan Falconer is a member of deck-audit's nine-card 'A Vampire lord or anthem drawn (the combat plan)' component whose 83.2% the verdict quotes as a strength, so the cut takes that component 9 -> 8 and the entry never prices it. difficulty 'contested' is right; the reason given for it is not.

The re-argued priority now rests on a substitution claim: 'trigger damage cannot be blocked, fogged or taxed by the Propaganda-shaped permanents that would otherwise be the reason to want it. A fifth payoff partly substitutes for a third answer; the reverse does not hold.' The generalisation outruns its own example set. axes[11] names four permanents only Anguished Unmaking can answer — Ghostly Prison, Propaganda, Rest in Peace, Torpor Orb. Three are genuinely routed around: the two taxes hit attacking and this deck kills by triggers, and the deck barely uses its graveyard (deck_recon.json records that the community's graveyard rebuild cards were excluded). Torpor Orb is not Propaganda-shaped: 'Creatures entering the battlefield don't cause abilities to trigger' is aimed at exactly the wording every member of the payoff class shares ('Whenever a creature you control enters'). If it applies, a fifth payoff is blanked alongside the other four and the answer slot is the ONLY thing that restores the primary kill — the substitution runs backwards for the one case that matters most. I am not asserting the ruling: no stack tests it, `deck-audit` cannot, and that is the point — the document's central ordering depends on a rules question it raises the example for and never asks. The hedges ('most of what that permanent would do', 'Propaganda-shaped') scope the claim but quietly exclude the worst case that the sibling axis explicitly includes. The ordering may well still be right on consequence; the argument as written does not establish it.

Unfixed from the previous iteration, and now internally inconsistent. The reading still says 'the audit's probe note lists six more the taxonomy filed elsewhere'. deck-audit's card-advantage axis carries EIGHT in measured.possible_uncounted: Castle Locthwain, Henrika Domnathi, Midgar City of Mako, Minas Tirith, Preacher of the Schism, Savai Triome, Silent Clearing, Sunbaked Canyon. Six is the count of the truncated notes[] string, which ends in an ellipsis. The add entry is the correct one (I verified all four oracle texts; Castle Locthwain and the two horizon lands draw with no board, though Savai Triome's is cycling from hand and is selection rather than advantage). The axis reading was left behind when the add was fixed.

The substance is real and I verified it independently and more sharply than the document states — but it is attached to an axis that measures something else, and the verdict label is false about the thing measured. The claim 'ANGUISHED UNMAKING IS THE DECK'S ONLY ANSWER to a Ghostly Prison, a Propaganda, a Rest in Peace or a Torpor Orb' is TRUE: I regex-scanned all 97 mainboard entries for removal wording, and the only cards that can touch a noncreature permanent are Anguished Unmaking (any nonland permanent) and Despark (mana value 4+); Ghostly Prison and Propaganda are mana value 3, Rest in Peace and Torpor Orb 2, so Despark reaches none of them. Everything else — Swords, Path, Winds of Abandon, Elspeth's -3, Henrika's edict — is creature-only. deck-audit's component agrees it is thin (size 2, thin true, thinnest true, 0.308 / 0.238, opening_seven 0.137). But the AXIS is interaction-breadth, its measured value is 5 classes answered against a low of 5, deck-audit's verdict is 'at', and the reading concedes it outright: 'All five classes are covered and uncovered is empty.' Rating an at-target axis 'weakness' on the strength of a different quantity mislabels the measurement — and it is what moved the validator's weak count 2 -> 3, so any reader or downstream consumer scanning verdicts without readings learns something false about breadth. The finding belongs on the engine component, which already flags it, or on axes[6], which actually counts answers and is rated 'adequate'. Not an artefact of the composition fix; a real weakness filed on the wrong row.

The headline correction is right and lands. The reading now re-derives from deck-audit's named card list rather than the count: it identifies the same five over-reads I did (Impact Tremors, Purphoros and Warleader's Call carrying removal:damage for 'deals 1 damage to each opponent' while being this diagnosis's own binding payoff class; Boros Charm's damage mode hitting a player or planeswalker; Elspeth being a multiplier), and 12 - 5 = 7 is arithmetically consistent with the seven it names. I checked the other direction for over-correction and it has not swung too far: my own independent list was also seven, differing only in membership — the doctor excludes Elspeth's -3 (genuine but conditional removal: destroy target creature an opponent controls with mana value 3 or greater, off a five-mana planeswalker) and includes Cemetery Gatekeeper's graveyard exile, where I did the reverse. Either composition gives 7, and at 8 the verdict would not move: 7 against the aggro override of 5-6 is at-to-slightly-over, 8 would be exactly Walser's '8-10 removal' floor, and 'adequate' is defensible on both. The exclusion of Elspeth is stated in the text so a reader can re-add her. The retraction in axes[11] — 'this diagnosis's earlier claim that the deck was over-invested in answers was wrong' — is explicit.

The priority order is now argued rather than restated, and it concedes what it must. The verdict states plainly that the noncreature answer is thinner on raw draw odds (two cards, 13.7% of openers — matching deck-audit's opening_seven 0.137 exactly, and 'functionally one against a cheap permanent' which I verified), and ranks the payoff class first on consequence rather than scarcity, with the tradeoff stated in both directions: a missing payoff is paid every game, a missing answer only when the permanent appears. open_questions[4] then labels the substitution reasoning as 'reasoning this diagnosis makes rather than quotes' and routes it to research-strategy. That is the correct disposition for an unquoted argument, and it is a real corpus hole — nothing in the strategy DB ranks two thin classes against each other. One observation rather than a finding: strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite already answers the depth half of that question with 'Breadth before depth ... Depth is a meta call: copy the answer your table beats you with', the phrase appears nowhere in the diagnosis, and deck_recon.json is the meta artifact that would settle it. The spawn is still justified by the ranking half; the corpus sentence should be engaged before it is made.

Generous Gift is the strongest entry in the document and its audit claim is exact. I checked it against the audit rather than accepting it: deck-audit's noncreature-answer component carries a closers block, and Generous Gift is FIRST in by_role, edhrec_rank 58, signature removal:spot, by_role_total 1091 — verbatim what the evidence block asserts. Its controller creates a 3/3 green Elephant creature token' — any permanent at any mana value at instant speed, which is precisely the gap Despark's mana-value-4 floor leaves, and the mana values quoted for Propaganda (3) and Torpor Orb (2) are correct. Colour identity is W, inside Mardu, Commander-legal, and it is in neither the mainboard nor the 29-entry sideboard. The 3/3 Elephant is named as the honest cost rather than omitted. The closers list is a role-signature route scoped to this component, and the entry argues from the card's text rather than leaning on the rank.
